THIS CRIMINAL APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 378(1) & (3) OF CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE, PRAYING TO GRANT LEAVE TO APPEAL AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND ORDER OF ACQUITTAL DATED 08.06.2015 PASSED BY THE SESSIONS JUDGE, YADGIRI, IN S.C.NO.62 OF 2012,
ACQUITTING THE RESPONDENTS FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 302, 304-B READ WITH SECTION 34 OF IPC.
(A) SET ASIDE THE AFORESAID JUDGMENT AND ORDER OF ACQUITTAL PASSED BY THE COURTS BELOW BY ALLOWING THIS APPEAL.
(B) CONVICT AND SENTENCE THE ACCUSED/RESPONDENT FOR THE OFFENCES PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 302, 304 READ WITH SECTION 34 OF IPC IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, IN THE INTEREST OF JUSTICE AND EQUITY.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
MOHAMMAD NAWAZ J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the State, aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 08.06.2015 passed by the Court of the Sessions Judge at Yadgiri, in Special Case No.62/2012, insofar as acquitting the respondents/accused Nos.1 to 3 of the offence punishable under Sections 302, 304-B R/w Section 34 of IPC.
2.

sentences.text:
Charges are framed against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A,
304-B and 302 R/w Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act R/w Section 34 of IPC NC: 2023:KHC-K:6437-DB 3.

The learned Sessions Judge convicted accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offence punishable under Section 498-A R/w Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 R/w Section 34 of IC.
4.
Insofar as the conviction and sentence passed against accused Nos.1 to 3, they preferred Criminal Appeal No.200068/2015 before this Court.
The said appeal was allowed in part vide judgment dated 21.04.2021.

The impugned judgment was set aside in part, whereby the accused were acquitted of the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 R/w 34 of IPC.
5.

In the present appeal, we are concerned with the challenge made to the impugned judgment insofar as acquittal of accused No.1 to 3 of the offence punishable under Sections 304-B and 302 The State Of Karnataka Through Kembhavi ... vs Sharnappa @ Shivasharanappa S/O ... on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65974832/
2 read with Section 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: We have heard the learned Addl. SPP appearing for the State and learned counsel appearing for the respondents.
7. Brief facts of the prosecution case are that, the marriage of deceased Shankramma @ Suvarna was solemnized with accused No.1 on 27.05.2011.
During the marriage, 2 1/2 tolas of gold and Rs.1,00,000/- in cash was demanded and accepted as dowry by the accused persons.
Three months after the marriage, the accused started subjecting the deceased to cruelty for the purpose of additional dowry of Rs.2,00,000/-.
The accused were coercing her to get additional dowry from her parental home, saying that the dowry given at the time of marriage was insufficient.
Panchayat was also held, but the accused continued to harass the deceased for the purpose of additional dowry.
On 10.03.2012 in the morning hours, the dead body of Shankramma was found floating in Indi canal in Hadanur village.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by PW5- brother of the deceased, PW20-PSI NC: 2023:KHC-K:6437-DB registered a case against the accused persons and issued the FIR-Ex.P6 to the jurisdictional Court.
Investigation was taken over by Dy.SP-PW-23.
The PM examination over the dead body was conducted by PW21.
On completion of investigation charge sheet was filed against the accused persons.

8. It is the case of prosecution that accused Nos.1 to 3 namely the husband and parents in law of the deceased Shankramma @ Suvarna demanded and accepted dowry of Rs.1,00,000/- in cash and 2  tolas of gold at the time of marriage and thereafter subjected her to cruelty for the purpose of additional dowry of Rs.2,00,000/-.
Charges were framed under Sections 498-A, 304-B as well as under Section 302 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
9. To establish that the accused persons have committed the murder, prosecution is mainly relying on the medical and circumstantial evidence, since, there are no eye witnesses to the incident.

One of the witness NC: 2023:KHC-K:6437-DB examined as PW15, who is supposed to have deposed with regard to the deceased last seen in the company of the accused, going towards the land on the date of incident has not supported the case of prosecution.
He has been treated hostile and nothing worthwhile has been elicited in his cross examination.
10. PW5, the first informant is the brother of the deceased.

In his complaint marked as Ex.P6, he has alleged that at the time of marriage, as per the talks, a cash of Rs.2,00,000/- and 5 tolas of gold was given and for about three months his sister was looked after properly by the accused persons.
Thereafter, the accused started demanding additional dowry of Rs.2,00,000/- and in this connection they were giving physical and mental torture to his sister.
He has stated that about a month prior to the date of incident, his sister had visited their village and at that time she informed about the cruelty meted to her by the accused persons.

sentences.text: FIR was registered against the husband, parents-in-law as well as the sister of accused No.1.
However, while filing charge sheet, the sister-in-law of the deceased, arraigned as accused No.4 in the FIR was dropped.

12. PW5 has stated that on 09.03.2012 at about 8.30 pm, his sister made a telephonic call informing that the accused are threatening her with dire consequences, if the amount was not brought from her parental home.

On the date of incident at about 11.30 a.m., the complainant went to the house of the accused and at that time his sister was not present and when he enquired with the accused persons, they informed him that they are not aware about her whereabouts.
Thereafter, he came to know from the villagers that the accused have taken his sister to the land and after committing the murder, threw her dead body into the canal.
13. As already noted supra, there are no eye witnesses, who have seen the accused committing the NC: 2023:KHC-K:6437-DB murder of Shankaramma @ Suvarna.
According to PW5, he heard from the villagers that the accused after committing the murder of his sister, threw the dead body in the canal.

One of the witness examined as PW15 has not supported the case of prosecution and therefore, it is not proved by the prosecution that the accused and deceased went to the land together on the date of incident.
PW5 to PW10 are hearsay witnesses and from their evidence it cannot be concluded that the accused have committed the murder and then threw her dead body into the canal.
14. PW21 is the medical officer who conducted the autopsy over the dead body.
Ex.P21 is the post mortem report.
As per the final opinion furnished by PW21, the cause of death is on account of cardio respiratory failure due to drowning.

15. The learned Addl. SPP has vehemently contended that there are certain injuries noticed while conducting the PM examination and even while drawing NC: 2023:KHC-K:6437-DB the inquest mahazar-Ex.P1, injuries were noticed on the dead body, which is spoken by the witnesses as well as the Tahasildar-PW16 who conducted the inquest proceedings.
He therefore, contended that it is a case of murder, wherein, the accused after assaulting the deceased have thrown the dead body in the canal.
16. It is relevant to see that PW21 has not deposed in his evidence that the death was on account of any injuries sustained by the deceased.
On the other hand in the cross examination, it is elicited by the defence that the injuries could have been caused by aquatic animals.
As per final opinion, cause of death is on account of cardio respiratory failure due to drowning.

Hence, the prosecution has failed to establish the charges leveled against the accused for the offence punishable under Section 302 R/w 34 of IPC.
17.

The prosecution is mainly relying on the evidence of PW5 to PW10 to establish that there was demand and acceptance of dowry at the time of marriage - 10 - The State Of Karnataka Through Kembhavi ... vs Sharnappa @ Shivasharanappa S/O ... on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65974832/
4 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6437-DB and that after the marriage, the accused were subjecting the deceased to cruelty for the purpose of additional dowry of Rs.2,00,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. In order to establish the charge under Section 304-B of IPC, the prosecution has to prove that the deceased was subjected to cruelty soon before her death.
In the case on hand, insofar as the injuries noticed on the dead body of the deceased is concerned, there is no evidence to show that the said injuries are caused by the accused persons.
On the other hand, the doctor-PW21 has stated that those injuries could have been caused by aquatic animals.
In the absence of any positive evidence, it cannot be held that the injuries were caused to the deceased by the accused persons soon before her death.

19. According to the prosecution, prior to the incident all the accused were coercing the deceased to get additional dowry of Rs.2,00,000/- from the house of the parents telling her that what was given at the time of marriage was not sufficient.

The learned Sessions Judge - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6437-DB has convicted accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A of IPC as well as under Section 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

As already noted supra, in the appeal preferred by the accused in Crl.A.No.200068/2015, the learned Single Judge was pleased to hold that the charges under Section 3 and 4 of Dowry prohibition Act, 1961 R/w 34 of IPC are not proved.
Accordingly, the accused were acquitted of the said offences.
It is relevant to extract para 33 of the said judgment.
"33. All these factors viewed cumulatively, the materials available on record is sufficient enough to convict the accused for the offence punishable under Section 498A IPC.
But the finding of the Trial Judge that accused are also to be convicted for the offences punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of the D.P.Act, cannot be maintained.
It is also pertinent to note that except at the time of marriage, no other amount is paid by the complainant to the accused as dowry.
The cash and gold given at the time of marriage would be treated as customary practice.

Accordingly, the Point No.1 is answered partly in the affirmative."
20.

The learned Sessions Judge while acquitting the accused of the offence under Section 304-B of IPC has observed that, on a perusal of the oral and documentary evidence led by the prosecution,
neither the prosecution knows nor the accused knows the reason for which Shankramma @ Suvarna falling down in the canal water as no-body have seen the actual falling of the deceased Shankramma @ Suvarna in canal water.

Even there is a possibility of the said Shankramma @ Suvarna falling The State Of Karnataka Through Kembhavi ... vs Sharnappa @ Shivasharanappa S/O ... on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65974832/
5 down in the canal water on account of slip of her legs.

entities.text: State Of Karnataka Through Kembhavi ... vs Sharnappa @ Shivasharanappa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 21. Having carefully examined the entire evidence and material on record, we are of the considered view that there is no sufficient material placed by the prosecution that soon before her death, the deceased was subjected to cruelty for the purpose of dowry, in connection with the marriage and on account of the said cruelty, she died. Further, the accused have been acquitted of the charges - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6437-DB under Section 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

The conviction insofar as Section 498-A of IPC is concerned, the same has been confirmed by this Court in Criminal Appeal No.200068/2015.
22.
This being an appeal against the judgment and order of acquittal passed by the Trial Court, we find no compelling or substantial reasons to reverse the said judgment.
It is trite law that, when two views are possible, then the one which favours the accused should be accepted.

23. For the foregoing reasons, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Appeal is dismissed.
